record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Assume that a word with length n, and containing k many distinct abelian-square factors, exists. Then a binary word of lengthn containing at least k many distinct abelian-square factors exists.

evidence.quote: Assume that a word with length n, and containing k many distinct abelian-square factors, exists. Then a binary word of lengthn containing at least k many distinct abelian-square factors exists. Two abelian squares are inequivalent if their Parikh vectors are different [28].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet. A word over $\Sigma$ is a finite sequence of letters of $\Sigma$. For a word $w$, the Parikh vector of $w$ is the vector indexing each letter $a \in \Sigma$ by the number of occurrences of $a$ in $w$. An abelian square is a word of the form $uv$ where $u$ and $v$ have the same Parikh vector (equivalently, $v$ is a permutation of $u$). Two abelian squares are considered inequivalent (distinct) if their Parikh vectors differ. A factor of a word $w$ is a contiguous subword of $w$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every integer $n \geq 1$ and every $k \geq 0$, if there exists a word of length $n$ over some finite alphabet that contains $k$ distinct abelian-square factors (counted up to equivalence of Parikh vectors), then there also exists a binary word (i.e., a word over a 2-letter alphabet) of length $n$ that contains at least $k$ distinct abelian-square factors.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is the Fici–Mignosi conjecture asserting that binary words maximize the number of distinct abelian-square factors. Subsequent works (e.g., on abelian-square-rich words by Fici, Mignosi, and Shallit) show that binary words attain Θ(n²) distinct abelian squares, which is the right order, but the literature does not indicate that the precise conjecture has been settled. Recent papers in 2026 still refer to the conjecture and only resolve special cases, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Abelian-Square-Rich Words
status_evidence.snippet: Studies binary words containing Θ(n²) distinct abelian-square factors, addressing the conjecture without fully resolving it.
status_evidence.claim: Binary words attain the right order Θ(n²) of distinct abelian squares, supporting but not fully proving the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Binary Words Containing Few Abelian Squares (2026)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper continuing the study of abelian squares in binary words.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of counting abelian squares in binary words remains active research as of 2026.
